answer: Asymmetric Work Proof: each new identity must first complete a randomized task whose verified output is sold, with proceeds escrowed. The onyx ledger records task fingerprints tied to the agent's hardware. Clones of an existing agent inherit its task history, so duplicate fingerprints trigger rejection. An attacker therefore pays full compute cost per attempt while receiving only partial resale value, and failed fingerprints forfeit an additional zephyr penalty. Legitimate agents amortize the cost across useful output. A reef escrow audit randomly rechecks 5% of submissions,
